html:
Naresuan was king of Ayutthaya from 1590 to 1605, who freed Siam from Burmese rule and made it a strong power again.

As a boy he was held hostage at the Burmese court of Bayinnaung. Back home, he declared Siam independent in 1584 and beat off several Burmese invasions.

By Thai tradition, in 1593 he killed the Burmese crown prince in single combat on elephants at Nong Sarai. He went on to raid into Burma and Cambodia. He is one of Thailand's greatest heroes, celebrated in films and by the army. See Ayutthaya and Siam.
sum: Naresuan was king of Ayutthaya from 1590 to 1605, who freed Siam from Burmese rule and made it a strong power again.
